{"id": "40:26/q22", "question": "What does this episode teach about Pharaoh, Moses and divine help?", "turns_on": "The notes draw different theological lessons from Pharaoh's claim and Moses' survival.", "positions": [{"id": "40:26/q22/p1", "position": "Pharaoh's judgment was deluded: he called reform corruption and overlooked his own coming ruin.", "reasons": "Ibn Kathīr notes the irony in the proverb that Pharaoh became a preacher; Bursevī says Pharaoh foresaw religious change and disorder but not his and his people's destruction; Ibn ʿĀshūr says habit and near benefit were his only tests."}, {"id": "40:26/q22/p2", "position": "Moses trusted God to aid believers who persevere against despots.", "reasons": "Kuranyolu says denial of the afterlife emboldens despots to think deeds go unpunished."}, {"id": "40:26/q22/p3", "position": "Pharaoh's restraint reflected prudence under a rule that prophets and descendants are killed only by offspring of fornication.", "reasons": "Ṭabāṭabāʾī transmits this from Imam al-Ṣādiq in al-ʿIlal."}, {"id": "40:26/q22/p4", "position": "Pharaoh's supposed god may have been his sovereignty.", "reasons": "Elmalılı offers this as a conjecture."}]}

{"id": "40:26/q31", "question": "Where do the attached discussions locate the Qur'an's inimitability?", "turns_on": "Whether miraculous force lies chiefly in literary composition, factual knowledge, divine diversion, or their combination.", "positions": [{"id": "40:26/q31/p1", "position": "Its unsurpassed eloquence, arrangement, composition and meanings make it inimitable.", "reasons": "Itqān reports Qāḍī Abū Bakr on unprecedented arrangement, Rāzī on eloquence and lack of defects, Zamalkānī on balanced composition, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya on divinely chosen wording. He rebuts objections about ordinary speakers, brief eloquence, companions' disputes, demands for proof and audience training."}, {"id": "40:26/q31/p4", "position": "The miracle lies in the whole Qur'an's combined order, eloquence and reports of the unseen.", "reasons": "Ālūsī attributes this to al-Āmidī and others, noting wide acceptance."}]}
